CausalChain: Nanoparticle engineered with boron compound + TLR agonist -> Preferential accumulation in tumor microenvironment -> BNCT irradiation produces high-LET particle mediated tumor cell death -> Release of tumor neoantigens and DAMPs -> TLR agonist enhances local innate immune activation -> Dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation -> Activation of tumor-specific T cells -> Systemic anti-tumor immune response and abscopal effect
Hypothesis: Conjugating boron delivery agents with TLR agonists into tumor-targeted nanoparticles will, when combined with BNCT, not only improve local tumor cell killing but also trigger a systemic anti-tumor immune response, leading to enhanced control of metastatic disease through an abscopal effect.
Abstract: Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) has been primarily developed as a localized cancer treatment by exploiting the selective uptake of boronated agents into tumor cells followed by the emission of high linear energy transfer particles upon neutron irradiation. Despite its localized cytotoxic effects, challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, suboptimal boron delivery and limited systemic tumor control persist. Here, we propose a novel approach combining targeted BNCT with immunomodulatory nanoparticle technology. By engineering nanoparticles that conjugate boron compounds with toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, it is hypothesized that BNCT‐induced immunogenic tumor cell death can be augmented. The resultant release of tumor neoantigens and damage associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) together with TLR stimulation could activate dendritic cells and promote a systemic T-cell mediated response. This integrated treatment strategy may not only enhance the local therapeutic ratio but also potentially induce an abscopal effect, controlling metastatic lesions and reducing recurrence.
